sections.heading: Basics
items: 4 players (you and 3 CPUs) with a 52-card deck (no jokers). One game decides the winner.
Each player starts with 3 cards. The top card of the deck is turned over as the starting card. The dealer is random. Play goes clockwise.
Card values: A = 1, 2–10 as printed, J = 11, Q = 12, K = 13.

sections.heading: Your turn
items: Play one card from your hand that has the same rank or the same suit as the top card. If you can play, you must.
If you cannot play, draw one card. After drawing, play if you can; otherwise pass.
With only 1 card in hand, draw first. You cannot go out by emptying your hand; the only way to win is Dobon.

sections.heading: Arming
items: When your hand total is 13 or less, press Arm to become armed. You cannot declare Dobon unless you are armed. Everyone can see who is armed.

You can press it for a few seconds at the start of the game and during your own turn. If you press it mid-turn, it is reserved: it is confirmed if your total is 13 or less when your play or pass is done, and fails if it is 14 or more.
If an armed player's total becomes 14 or more, the arm is removed automatically. You cannot remove it yourself.

sections.heading: Dobon
items: While armed, when your hand total equals the rank of the top card, flick the Dobon button upward to declare. A simple tap does not declare.
Only cards played by other players count. The starting card and cards you played yourself do not. Matching the total by drawing does not count either.
You can declare from right after a card is played until the next player makes their first action.
A valid Dobon ends the game: the declarer wins and the player who played that card loses. If several players declare, the one closest clockwise after the player who played wins.

sections.heading: Foul
items: Declaring Dobon when your total does not match is a foul. The player who fouled loses and the game ends.
If a Dobon and a foul happen together, the Dobon takes priority.

sections.heading: End of the game
items: The game ends on a Dobon or a foul. If the deck runs out and a player cannot draw, it is a no contest.
